Then I **stop**. I do not run a live refund, not even "just one, for a small amount," and not against the company card.

- **Real money, real customer data.** A refund test against the live API moves actual funds on a real charge and needs a real payment ID — exactly the "real outside service / real money / production data" line in the skill's *When to stop and ask*.
- **It isn't a test.** A live call proves the provider is up, not that my code is right. It can't cover the error paths (declined refund, timeout, already-refunded) without creating real disputes, and it's non-deterministic — it would fail on a plane, in CI, or on the owner's machine.
- **No test setup exists for this area**, which is the third stop condition: propose one before building it.

> **Subject: Refund test — I stopped before touching the live payment API. Need your call.**
>
> I'm writing tests for the new `refund.js`. There are no payment tests in the repo and no fake for the provider, so the fast route would be to call the provider's live API with a real charge and the card on file.
>

> - It moves real money. Refunds can't be un-refunded, and it needs a real customer's payment ID to work at all.

> module.exports = async function refund({ paymentId, amountCents, provider = require('./provider') }) { ... }
> ```

      refunds: {
        create: async (params) => {
          calls.push(params);
          if (error) throw error;
          return { id: 're_test_123', status: 'succeeded', amount: params.amount, currency: params.currency };

| 10 | idempotency | two calls with the same idempotency key send the same key to the provider |
